headline: This man couldn't
body: His testosterone was normal. His bones were falling apart.
punch: And he was still growing as an adult.

headline: Last time
body: A man whose estrogen receptor didn't work never stopped growing. This is the other half of that experiment — same outcome, different break in the chain.
punch: One couldn't read the signal. This one couldn't make it.

headline: He had aromatase deficiency
body: Aromatase converts androgens into estrogen. Without it, testosterone stays testosterone. His androgen levels were normal to high and none of it became estradiol.
punch: Plenty of hormone. None of the conversion.

headline: The result
body: Unfused epiphyses. Open growth plates in an adult. And low bone mass, despite testosterone levels that should have built strong bone on their own.
punch: Normal androgens did not protect his skeleton.

headline: Then they gave him
body: Bone mineral density increased substantially. The deficit that normal testosterone had failed to prevent was corrected by adding the hormone he couldn't produce.
punch: This is the treatment arm the receptor case couldn't have.

headline: Which is why
body: The estrogen-receptor patient proved the signal is necessary. This one proved supplying it works — because his receptors were fine, only the supply was broken.
punch: Two natural experiments. Same conclusion from opposite directions.

headline: So for male bone
body: Testosterone matters largely because of what it gets converted into. Estradiol appears necessary to maximise bone health in men — not incidental to it.
punch: Androgen is the raw material. Estrogen does the work.

headline: The honest caveat
body: These are single-patient case reports. Extraordinarily informative, because the variable is isolated by genetics rather than by design — but still n of one.
punch: The cleanest evidence available is not the same as large evidence.

headline: It's never over
body: Real mechanisms, real citations, no protocols.
